planting.note: Plant in fall or spring in a site with morning sun and afternoon shade to extend flower life and protect buds from hard freezes.

directions: 'Shinonome' is one of the classic representative cultivars of the true Sasanqua Group, the class of camellias that stay closest to the wild species. It bears single flowers of five to eleven petals in white-to-pink tones from October into December, with prominent golden stamens and light fragrance. Grow it as an understory specimen or informal hedge where dappled shade shelters the autumn blooms from scorching; it tolerates clipping well. Fertile, humus-rich, acidic soil with consistent moisture produces the best bloom set.

planting.note: Site in part shade with protection from drying winter wind to keep autumn flowers from browning.

directions: Like 'Shinonome', 'Tai-shuhai' is cited as a representative cultivar of the true Sasanqua Group, retaining the wild species' character: single, lightly fragrant flowers of white, pink, or red opening October through December above glossy dark evergreen foliage. Its vigorous, upright-to-spreading habit suits foundation plantings or a loose woodland-edge hedge beneath high deciduous canopy. Water during dry autumn spells to support flower bud development and avoid planting in heavy, poorly drained soils.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Give filtered light under high shade; the dense dull foliage tends to scald in exposed full-sun sites.

directions: 'Tago-no-tsuki' is the representative cultivar of the Oleifera Group of sasanqua-type camellias, which carry Camellia oleifera parentage. It is marked by large, dull-surfaced evergreen leaves and small, simple white flowers, a quieter floral display than typical sasanquas but a tougher, more cold- and disease-resilient constitution. Use it as a background screening shrub in a shaded border where the modest blooms are a bonus rather than the main event. Mulch well to keep roots cool and moist through summer.

planting.note: Plant where afternoon shade protects the pale, single petals from fading and sun-scorch.

directions: 'Moon Mist' produces light pink, single-layer-petaled flowers over a long fall-into-winter season, making it a softer-colored companion to the more common deep-pink and red sasanquas. The glossy evergreen foliage stays dense and tidy on a rounded, moderately sized frame well suited to a shaded foundation planting or informal screen. It performs best with consistent moisture and acidic, well-drained soil, and benefits from light pruning right after bloom to maintain shape.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Blooms slightly earlier than 'Narumigata'; site in part shade to lengthen the display before hard frost.

directions: 'Fukuzu-tsumi' closely resembles the well-known 'Narumigata' but flowers roughly two weeks earlier, opening large single white blooms edged in soft pink from early autumn. It is a reliable, floriferous grower reported to perform especially well in cool, humid climates, making it a dependable choice for a shaded shrub border or specimen beneath high canopy. Deadhead spent flowers to tidy the display and keep soil evenly moist but never waterlogged.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

planting.note: Site in part shade; profuse white-blush bloom holds its color longer out of direct afternoon sun.

directions: 'Autumn White' was selected for exceptionally profuse white-to-blush blooming in fall, giving a fuller flower display than many single-flowered sasanquas of similar color. Its dense evergreen habit works well as a flowering screen or background shrub along a shaded woodland edge. Provide acidic, well-drained soil amended with organic matter, and water during dry spells in late summer to support bud set.

planting.note: Use as a tidy evergreen edger or mass groundcover in dense shade beneath established trees.

directions: 'Margie Jenkins', named for the Louisiana nurserywoman who selected it, is a notably dwarf, compact form of coastal doghobble that stays well under knee height, far smaller than the species or most other named axillaris clones. Glossy, leathery evergreen leaves arch gracefully from low mounding stems, and small white urn-shaped flowers appear in spring along the branch undersides. It is an excellent low edging or small-scale groundcover for deep, moist shade where taller leucothoes would overwhelm the scale of the planting. Keep soil consistently moist and acidic for best foliage color.
sources: North Carolina Extension Gardener Plant Toolbox

planting.note: Plant a male skimmia nearby to ensure pollination and fruit set on this female clone.

directions: 'Fructo-Albo' is an old, distinct female Skimmia japonica clone grown for its creamy-white berries, a striking departure from the usual red-fruited female cultivars like 'Nymans' or 'Veitchii'. Its dense, mounding evergreen habit and leathery dark leaves make it a dependable low shrub for a shaded border, and the pale fruit persists well into winter against the dark foliage. Grow it in humus-rich, reliably moist, acidic soil in full to partial shade, mirroring the needs of other skimmia cultivars.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)

planting.note: Pair with a female clone such as 'Nymans' to guarantee a heavy berry set.

directions: 'Ruby Dome' is an improved male Skimmia japonica selection noted as an effective pollinator for free-fruiting female clones such as 'Nymans', producing the fragrant, rounded flower clusters typical of male skimmias but with crisper, more floriferous panicles. As a male plant it bears no fruit itself but provides essential pollination for berries elsewhere in the shade bed while contributing dense, dome-shaped evergreen structure year-round. Grow in cool, moist, humus-rich acidic soil sheltered from drying wind and hot afternoon sun.
sources: Trees and Shrubs Online (International Dendrology Society)
